Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

hate verb

also can’t stand, loathe

classical

Catull. 85.1
Traupman 153, 326

ōdī, ōdisse

verb, defective: perfect in form, present in meaning

Ōdī, I hate; ōderam, I hated; ōderō, I shall hate. With an infinitive too (Hor. Ep. 1.16.52, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • ōdī et amō. quārē id faciam, fortasse requīris.

    I hate and I love. Why do I do it, you may ask.Catull. 85.1

  • ōdimus accipitrem, quia vīvit semper in armīs

    we hate the hawk, because it lives always armedOv. Ars 2.147

  • Omnīnō ōdī surgere tam bene māne.

    I absolutely hate getting up so early.Traupman 35

Other words

  • fastīdiō, fastīdīre, fastīdīvī, fastīdītum — turn up one’s nose at, loathe (food above all)

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Men. 1.2.58: ut fastīdīs! (Lewis & Short); Hor. Ep. 1.17.15 (Lewis & Short)

    The fussy eater’s verb: Lewis & Short, “to shrink or flinch from any thing unpleasant to the taste”. Not frequent before Augustus.

  • abhorreō, abhorrēre, abhorruī — shrink from, be set against

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Hec. 4.4.92: ā nūptiīs (Lewis & Short)

    With ab: a milder way to say “I hate”.

See also I love you, yucky.

SourcesLewis & Short: odi · Lewis & Short: fastidio · Lewis & Short: abhorreo
